title: The Power of Compound Interest
subtitle: Understand how time and reinvested returns turn small habits into wealth.

steps.content: Albert Einstein reportedly called compound interest the eighth wonder of the world. Let's see why it is so powerful!
steps.tip: Starting five years earlier can double your eventual retirement fund.

steps.title: Simple vs Compound Interest
steps.content:
Simple Interest: You earn interest only on your initial deposit (principal).

Compound Interest: You earn interest on your principal plus all previously accumulated interest!

Over 20–30 years, compound interest creates exponential growth.
steps.highlight: Compound interest makes your money work for you 24/7.

steps.question: What is the key mechanism that makes compound interest grow exponentially over time?
steps.hint: Unlike simple interest, compound interest reinvests previous earnings so your investment base grows on top of itself.

options.text: Earning returns on previous returns in addition to the principal deposit
options.explanation: Because each period's earnings are reinvested, the base on which future gains are calculated keeps expanding.

options.text: Doubling your monthly contributions every single month
options.explanation: Exponential growth occurs through reinvestment, even with flat monthly contributions.

options.text: Taking high-risk lottery bets with your capital
options.explanation: Gambling destroys wealth; disciplined compounding creates steady exponential gains.

steps.title: The Rule of 72
steps.content:
Want to know how fast your money will double? Divide 72 by your expected annual rate of return.

Example: At a 7% return, 72 / 7 is approximately 10.3 years to double your money without adding a single extra penny!
steps.highlight: Rule of 72: Years to double = 72 / Annual Return Rate.

steps.question: According to the Rule of 72, if your investments earn an average return of 8% annually, about how many years will it take to double?
steps.hint: Use the Rule of 72 shortcut: divide 72 by the annual return rate (8).

options.explanation: 72 divided by 8 equals 9 years to double your investment.
At 8%, 18 years would quadruple your balance instead of doubling.
Doubling in 5 years would require a much higher return of 14.4%.

steps.title: Compound Growth Mastered
steps.content: Time is your greatest financial superpower. Start early, stay consistent, and let compounding do the heavy lifting.
